name: application-pipeline-flow-node
title: Pipeline Flow Node
description: A draggable workflow-canvas process node with input/output connector ports, an icon, title, and a status indicator, shown connected to a downstream node.
useWhen: Building a workflow/automation builder (ETL pipeline, no-code automation, data pipeline) with a drag-and-drop node canvas.
Each step needs to show connection points (input/output ports) and a live execution status.
avoidWhen: You need to show proportional flow volume between stages, not a step-by-step process graph — `Sankey Flow Diagram` fits that instead.
The workflow has no branching/connection structure — a linear `Stepper Wizard` or `Steps` component is simpler.
responsiveBehavior: Each node keeps a fixed width regardless of container size; the canvas itself should be a pannable/zoomable surface in a real implementation rather than reflowing at narrow widths.
accessibility: Each node's icon is paired with a text title, and its status dot is paired with a text label ("Success", "Running"), not color alone.
The drag handle is the whole node body; in a real implementation, provide an equivalent keyboard-operable way to reorder or connect nodes.
Connector ports are decorative visual anchors; the underlying connection data should be exposed via accessible means (e.g. a text list of pipeline steps) alongside the canvas.

variants.title: Connected nodes
variants.description: Two workflow nodes ('Fetch Records' with a Success status, 'Transform' with a pulsing Running status) on a dotted canvas, connected by an arrow edge, each with visible input/output ports.
accessibility: Each node's status is stated as text ("Success", "Running") beside its indicator dot.

variants.title: Connected nodes (Dark)
variants.description: Pipeline flow nodes adapted for dark surfaces, including the canvas dot-grid and node status colors.
accessibility: Node borders, ports, and status text all meet WCAG AA contrast against the dark canvas background.
